extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from XML/PDF abstract, mechanism section, Table 6, Figure 1/3/4/5 captions, and methods for PI uptake, DiBAC4 depolarization, and SEM. Mechanism is accepted as membrane-targeting with explicit non-target caveats.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: YZ105 against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus USA300 LAC
mechanism_claims.claim_text: YZ105 rapidly reduces viable MRSA counts under 4x MIC killing-kinetics conditions, supporting bactericidal activity but not by itself identifying a molecular target.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Killing kinetics is treated as bactericidal phenotype evidence; membrane targeting is supported by the PI uptake, depolarization, and SEM claims below.

direct_assay_types: real-time propidium iodide membrane integrity assay
mechanism_claims.claim_text: YZ105 permeabilizes S. aureus USA300 membranes in the PI uptake assay, while inactive YZ103 and nonmembrane antibiotics do not show the same fluorescence response.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The prose includes an apparent YZ135 typo; figure caption and surrounding context identify YZ105 at 4 uM.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: YZ105 depolarizes S. aureus USA300 membranes to a positive-control-like extent, while nafcillin and linezolid remain negative controls in the source figure/prose.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Depolarization supports membrane targeting; it does not specify a single membrane binding target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM images show damaged bacterial cell surfaces after YZ105 treatment, providing direct morphology evidence consistent with membrane disruption.
mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM supports surface damage but does not distinguish all possible downstream lytic events.
